The Supreme Court has ruled that police have no specific obligation to protect an individual but do have a duty to protect the community at large. The ruling case on this matter dates back to 1981 in the Warren v District of Columbia case. There are several others, but for purposes of this response, I am sticking with this case as it is most relevant.

In this particular school shooting case, it is alleged by the plaintiff that one has a constitutional right to safety and that the police are the ones who are supposed to ensure that safety. Contrary to popular myth, the constitution does NOT, in any way, state that the government has a responsibility to the people to protect them (outside of maintaining an Army and Navy but even that does not guarantee safety, it only ensures that we can defend our borders and protect our interests). This is one of those areas of law where there simply isn't a "right" or "correct" answer. The police are obligated to protect the community as a whole but not an individual who is not in their custody. Yet, the community is made up of individuals. So, how to you proceed? It simply isn't possible to protect all the individuals of a community no matter how small the community and/or how large the police force. Even if you had a community of 100 people and every one of them were police officers, you simply cannot guarantee any individual's personal safety.

What it comes down to is this simple and unalterable fact: an individual's safety is their OWN responsibility.
